Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — appreciate the clarity on your ingestion flow and the retention constraints for transaction metadata. Per our call, I wanted to summarize what we discussed and outline next steps so we can get you a concise proposal and a short technical appendix for your security team.

Recap (from call):
- FintechCo will be ingesting enriched transaction text and some metadata (trace IDs, headers).
- You require PII redaction for request/response bodies and strict controls around logs and trace identifiers.
- Retention: staging logs <= 30 days; production aggregated metrics 13 months; raw request logs have stricter access controls and optional short retention.

What Redwood can provide (high-level):
- Request/response redaction at ingest with configurable policies (regexp + structured field redaction).
- Header scrubbing options (drop or allowlist headers) and trace ID hashing or full removal.
- Configurable retention per environment with automated purge, plus long-term aggregated metrics export.
- Audit logs & access controls tied to KMS-backed keys; SOC2 artifacts available on request.

Next steps:
1) Dev to share a short technical note on how redaction and header controls look in runtime config (will attach).
2) Security: we can provide SOC2 summary + deployment architecture for private/VPC options.
3) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your security engineer; suggested slots Thursday/Friday.

I've attached a short overview (redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf) and a tech-spec spreadsheet we can fill in.

Thanks —

Hi Alice — quick technical answers and example configs below. Happy to jump on the follow-up with your security engineer.

1) Hashing vs removal for trace IDs:
- We support configurable hash functions (SHA256) with salted per-customer keys (stored in KMS). Hashing is one-way and non-reversible.
- Optionally we can drop trace IDs entirely. Hashing allows correlation for performance debugging without exposing raw IDs.

2) Header scrubbing:
- Default deny-list approach for sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Internal-Auth).
- Allowlist mode available — only headers you list will be kept.

3) Redaction timing (client vs server):
- We recommend server-side redaction at the edge (ingest) so you get consistent behavior across SDKs and retries.
- We also provide a client-side SDK helper that applies the same redaction rules before sending if you prefer defense-in-depth.

4) Retention & deletions:
- Per-environment retention policies are configurable (e.g., staging: 30d, prod-raw: 90d, prod-aggregated: 13 months).
- We support per-request deletion API for legal hold requests — deletion is propagated and background-compacted; we provide an audit entry for the deletion event.

Example runtime snippet (pseudo-config):

redaction_policy:
  mode: server_ingest
  fields:
    - name: ssn
      pattern: "\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b"
      action: redact
  headers:
    mode: allowlist
    allow: ["Content-Type", "X-Request-Id"]
  trace_id:
    action: hash
    algorithm: sha256
    key_ref: projects/fintechco/key1

Notes: hash key rotation is supported; old hashes remain valid for correlation if we keep a key alias history for a configurable window.

Attachments: redaction-tech-specs.xlsx (contains the sample config and mapping table).
